newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-SOHAIL LIFTS PAKISTAN TO 223 ALL OUT.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-SOHAIL LIFTS PAKISTAN TO 223 ALL OUT.

text.p: Pakistan opener Aamir Sohail scored a patient 67 to lift his side to 223 all out in 49.5 overs against Australia in a World Series limited-overs match on Sunday.
Sohail laid the foundation for a competitive total by hitting six fours and one six in an innings lasting 131 minutes and 96 balls at Adelaide Oval.
But the tourists would have been disappointed to lose their last six wickets for 32 runs in a late collapse as they attempted to lift the scoring rate in the final 10 overs.
Wrist spinner Shane Warne took the last two wickets in successive balls to wrap up the innings and finish with the relatively expensive figures of four for 52 from 9.5 overs.
Australia, who beat West Indies in the opening two fixtures of the triangular tournament, need to score at a rate of little more than four runs an over to win in ideal conditions for batting.
Sohail combined with number three Mohammad Wasim to add 102 runs for the second wicket after captain and fast bowler Wasim Akram won the toss.
Wasim, playing in only his third limited-overs international, contributed 44 in 86 balls.
Their partnership was broken by makeshift left-arm wrist spinner Michael Bevan, who lured Sohail into edging a catch to wicketkeeper Ian Healy.
Bevan, who took two for 32 in eight overs, removed Wasim five balls later to halt Pakistan's momentum after they appeared poised to build a big total at 141 for one at one stage.
